questions.prompt: Which set shows the main areas combined in Pre-Technical Studies?
questions.correctAnswer: Business, computer, and technical studies
questions.explanation: Pre-Technical Studies introduces learners to business, computer, and technical skills for practical problem solving.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the components of Pre-Technical Studies as a learning area.

questions.prompt: Why is Pre-Technical Studies useful in day-to-day life?
options: It helps learners make, repair, communicate, and manage resources
It replaces all other subjects in junior school
It teaches learners to avoid teamwork
It only prepares learners for office writing
questions.correctAnswer: It helps learners make, repair, communicate, and manage resources
questions.explanation: The subject develops practical, digital, and entrepreneurial skills that can be used at home, school, and work.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of Pre-Technical Studies in day-to-day life.

questions.prompt: Which career is closely linked to technical skills learned in Pre-Technical Studies?
questions.correctAnswer: Carpenter
questions.explanation: Carpentry uses measuring, marking, materials, tools, safety, and production skills introduced in the subject.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate Pre-Technical Studies to career development.

questions.prompt: A learner designs a simple phone stand from waste cardboard. Which value of Pre-Technical Studies is best shown?
options: Creativity in solving a practical problem
questions.correctAnswer: Creativity in solving a practical problem
questions.explanation: Designing a useful item from available materials applies creativity, resource use, and production thinking.
questions.learningOutcome: Appreciate the role of Pre-Technical Studies in solving practical problems.

questions.prompt: Which statement best shows a learner embracing Pre-Technical Studies for career development?
options: I will practise safe tool use and learn how products are made
I will ignore practical tasks because they are not useful
I will only watch others working with tools
I will avoid learning about money and business
questions.correctAnswer: I will practise safe tool use and learn how products are made
questions.explanation: Career readiness grows when learners practise skills, safety, teamwork, and responsible use of resources.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate a positive attitude toward Pre-Technical Studies and career pathways.

questions.prompt: Which item is personal protective equipment for a learner using hand tools?
questions.correctAnswer: Safety goggles
questions.explanation: Safety goggles protect the eyes from dust, chips, and other small particles during practical work.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify personal protective equipment used during practical activities.

questions.prompt: What should a learner do first after noticing a loose electric cable in the workshop?
options: Report it to the teacher immediately
Touch it to check whether it is live
questions.correctAnswer: Report it to the teacher immediately
questions.explanation: Electrical hazards should be reported and isolated by a responsible person to prevent electric shock or fire.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe responses to hazards in the immediate environment.

questions.prompt: Which action helps prevent accidents in a practical work area?
options: Keeping tools and materials in their correct places
Leaving sharp tools on the floor
Using a tool before learning how it works
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping tools and materials in their correct places
questions.explanation: Good housekeeping reduces trips, cuts, and confusion when learners are carrying out practical tasks.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe safe practices for organising the work area.

questions.prompt: A small fire starts in a waste-paper bin. Which action is safest for a Grade 7 learner?
options: Raise the alarm and follow the teacher's instructions
Carry the burning bin across the room
questions.correctAnswer: Raise the alarm and follow the teacher's instructions
questions.explanation: Learners should alert others and follow emergency procedures instead of taking risky action alone.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain appropriate action during an emergency in the immediate environment.

questions.prompt: Which hazard is most likely caused by a wet floor near a workshop entrance?
questions.correctAnswer: Slipping and falling
questions.explanation: A wet floor reduces grip under the feet, so it can easily cause slips and falls.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common hazards in the school environment.

questions.prompt: Why should a learner read safety signs before using a room or tool?
options: Safety signs warn about risks and required precautions
Safety signs are used only for decoration
Safety signs make tools work faster
questions.correctAnswer: Safety signs warn about risks and required precautions
questions.explanation: Safety signs communicate hazards, instructions, and protective measures that reduce accidents.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret safety signs used in practical environments.

questions.prompt: Which pair shows the best safety practice and its reason?
options: Wear an apron; it protects clothes and skin from dirt and minor splashes
Wear open sandals; they make running easier
Share one pair of goggles; it saves time
Leave bags on the floor; they keep materials close
questions.correctAnswer: Wear an apron; it protects clothes and skin from dirt and minor splashes
questions.explanation: Protective clothing reduces exposure to dirt, small particles, and light splashes during practical work.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate safety practices to the risks they reduce.

questions.prompt: A class is arranging a safe workshop exit route. Which choice is most important?
options: Keep the exit clear of stools, bags, and materials
Place heavy boxes next to the exit
Use the exit area to store timber
Decorate the exit sign with paper strips
questions.correctAnswer: Keep the exit clear of stools, bags, and materials
questions.explanation: A clear exit allows people to leave quickly and safely during an emergency.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan safe movement in practical work areas.

questions.prompt: Which response best shows responsible first-aid behaviour after a learner gets a small cut?
options: Inform the teacher and use the first-aid kit under guidance
Ignore the cut and continue using tools
Wash the cut with paint thinner
Let several learners touch the wound
questions.correctAnswer: Inform the teacher and use the first-aid kit under guidance
questions.explanation: Minor injuries should be reported and cleaned safely to reduce infection and further harm.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply basic first-aid responses to minor injuries.

questions.prompt: Which part of a computer is mainly used to enter letters and numbers?
questions.correctAnswer: Keyboard
questions.explanation: A keyboard is an input device used to type letters, numbers, symbols, and commands.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common computer input devices.

questions.prompt: Which sequence best shows how a computer works with data?
questions.correctAnswer: Input, processing, output, storage
questions.explanation: A computer receives data, processes it, gives output, and may store results for later use.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the basic data processing cycle.

questions.prompt: Which example is data before processing?
options: Marks listed for each learner in a class
The class average calculated from marks
questions.correctAnswer: Marks listed for each learner in a class
questions.explanation: Raw marks are data; after calculation and organisation, they become useful information such as averages and summaries.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish between data and information in computing.

questions.prompt: Which habit helps protect a learner's computer account?
options: Writing the password on a classroom wall
Using the learner's name as the only password
questions.correctAnswer: Using a strong private password
questions.explanation: A strong private password helps prevent unauthorised access to files and accounts.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply basic data safety practices when using computers.

questions.prompt: Which storage device can be used to carry a small digital drawing file from home to school?
questions.correctAnswer: USB flash drive
questions.explanation: A USB flash drive stores digital files and can be moved between compatible computers.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common digital storage devices.

questions.prompt: A learner sits very close to the monitor and bends the back for a long time. Which risk is most likely?
questions.correctAnswer: Eye strain and poor posture
questions.explanation: Correct sitting position and suitable viewing distance help reduce discomfort and strain during computer use.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain ergonomic practices for safe computer use.

questions.prompt: Which option best protects files from being lost when a computer fails?
options: Keeping a backup copy in a safe storage location
Deleting old file names every day
Opening the same file many times
questions.correctAnswer: Keeping a backup copy in a safe storage location
questions.explanation: Backups provide another copy of important files in case the original is lost, damaged, or accidentally deleted.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of backup in data safety.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of technical drawing?
options: To communicate the shape and size of an object clearly
To decorate a page with random patterns
To hide measurements from the maker
questions.correctAnswer: To communicate the shape and size of an object clearly
questions.explanation: Technical drawing uses lines, symbols, and dimensions so that an object can be understood or made accurately.
questions.learningOutcome: State the purpose of drawing in technical communication.

questions.prompt: Which tool is most suitable for drawing a straight horizontal line in a technical drawing?
questions.correctAnswer: Ruler
questions.explanation: A ruler helps draw straight lines and measure lengths on paper.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify basic drawing tools and their uses.

questions.prompt: Which information is normally written in the title block of a drawing?
options: Name of the drawing, scale, date, and drawer's name
Only the price of the final product
Only the names of all classmates
questions.correctAnswer: Name of the drawing, scale, date, and drawer's name
questions.explanation: A title block records important details that identify and explain the drawing.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the information included in a drawing title block.

questions.prompt: Why should drawing instruments be kept clean and dry?
options: To produce neat accurate drawings and prevent damage
To change the size of the paper
questions.correctAnswer: To produce neat accurate drawings and prevent damage
questions.explanation: Clean tools make clear lines and last longer when they are handled and stored properly.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain care and maintenance of basic drawing instruments.

questions.prompt: A learner wants to show the actual measured size of a box edge on a drawing. Which drawing feature should be added?
questions.correctAnswer: Dimension
questions.explanation: A dimension shows a measured size such as length, width, or height on a drawing.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the use of dimensions in drawings.

questions.prompt: Which practice improves neatness when preparing a technical drawing?
options: Using sharp pencils and light construction lines
Pressing a blunt pencil very hard
Folding the drawing paper before use
questions.correctAnswer: Using sharp pencils and light construction lines
questions.explanation: Sharp pencils and light guide lines make it easier to produce accurate, clean drawings.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply good drawing practices to produce neat work.

questions.prompt: What is free-hand sketching?
options: Drawing without using instruments for every line
Printing a document from a computer
questions.correctAnswer: Drawing without using instruments for every line
questions.explanation: Free-hand sketching communicates an idea quickly using the hand, eye, and simple proportion control.
questions.learningOutcome: Define free-hand sketching in technical communication.

questions.prompt: Which situation best requires a quick free-hand sketch?
options: Explaining a design idea before making a model
questions.correctAnswer: Explaining a design idea before making a model
questions.explanation: A sketch helps others understand a design idea before detailed drawings or production begin.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain uses of free-hand sketches in design communication.

questions.prompt: Which feature makes a free-hand sketch easier to understand?
options: Clear outline, labels, and simple dimensions
Very dark smudges over all details
questions.correctAnswer: Clear outline, labels, and simple dimensions
questions.explanation: A useful sketch should show the main shape, named parts, and important sizes clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify qualities of a clear free-hand sketch.

questions.prompt: When sketching a rectangular stool, which step should come first?
options: Block out the general shape lightly
Add final dark lines before planning
Colour the legs before drawing them
Write the price before showing the shape
questions.correctAnswer: Block out the general shape lightly
questions.explanation: Lightly planning the overall shape helps keep the sketch proportionate before details are added.
questions.learningOutcome: Sequence the steps used in preparing a free-hand sketch.

questions.prompt: A learner's sketch of a cup looks too wide compared with its height. What should the learner improve?
questions.correctAnswer: Proportion
questions.explanation: Proportion is the relationship between sizes of parts, such as width compared with height.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply proportion when making free-hand sketches.

questions.prompt: Which kind of line is best for the final visible outline of a sketch?
questions.correctAnswer: A clear continuous line
questions.explanation: A visible outline should be clear and continuous so the object shape can be read easily.
questions.learningOutcome: Use suitable line quality in free-hand sketches.

questions.prompt: Which addition would make a free-hand sketch of a simple bookshelf more useful for production?
options: Labels for shelves, side panels, and approximate dimensions
questions.correctAnswer: Labels for shelves, side panels, and approximate dimensions
questions.explanation: Labels and dimensions guide the maker on parts, sizes, and arrangement of the item.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate sketch details needed for making a simple item.

questions.prompt: Why is it useful to sketch several possible designs before choosing one?
options: It helps compare ideas and improve the final solution
It guarantees that no material will be needed
questions.correctAnswer: It helps compare ideas and improve the final solution
questions.explanation: Several sketches allow learners to compare strengths and weaknesses before selecting a practical design.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare alternative sketches for a practical design problem.

questions.prompt: A learner must design a simple desk organiser for pens and rulers. What is the best sketching plan?
options: Draw the overall shape, label compartments, and show approximate sizes
Start cutting cardboard without a sketch
Write only the learner's name on the paper
questions.correctAnswer: Draw the overall shape, label compartments, and show approximate sizes
questions.explanation: A clear design sketch shows form, function, and size before materials are cut.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a sketching plan for a simple functional product.

questions.prompt: Which ICT tool is best for typing and editing a short report about a class project?
questions.correctAnswer: Word processor
questions.explanation: A word processor is software used to create, edit, format, and save text documents.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify ICT tools used for written communication.

questions.prompt: Which ICT tool would best help a group present photos and key points about a production project?
questions.correctAnswer: Presentation software
questions.explanation: Presentation software helps organise slides with text, images, charts, and speaking points.
questions.learningOutcome: Select appropriate ICT tools for presenting project information.

questions.prompt: Which action shows responsible digital communication?
options: Using polite language and checking facts before sharing
questions.correctAnswer: Using polite language and checking facts before sharing
questions.explanation: Responsible digital communication is respectful, accurate, and protects other people's privacy.
questions.learningOutcome: Practise responsible use of ICT tools in communication.

questions.prompt: Why should a learner give a clear file name to a saved drawing?
options: It makes the file easier to identify and retrieve later
It stops the drawing from needing measurements
questions.correctAnswer: It makes the file easier to identify and retrieve later
questions.explanation: Clear file names help users find, organise, and share digital work accurately.
questions.learningOutcome: Organise digital communication files using clear file names.

questions.prompt: A group wants to send a project report to the teacher electronically. Which method is most suitable where internet is available?
options: Attach the document to an email or approved learning platform
Hide the document in a toolbox
Write the password on the notice board
questions.correctAnswer: Attach the document to an email or approved learning platform
questions.explanation: Email and approved learning platforms can send digital files quickly when used safely and responsibly.
questions.learningOutcome: Use ICT tools to share project information appropriately.

questions.prompt: Which information should not be shared in a public class chat group?
options: The list of materials assigned by the teacher
questions.correctAnswer: A learner's private password
questions.explanation: Passwords are private security details and should not be shared in public or group messages.
questions.learningOutcome: Protect personal information when communicating digitally.

questions.prompt: Which choice best combines ICT and drawing communication for a class project?
options: Scan or photograph the sketch, label it clearly, and include it in a report
Throw away the sketch after drawing it
Send only a blank slide to the teacher
Use unrelated music instead of project details
questions.correctAnswer: Scan or photograph the sketch, label it clearly, and include it in a report
questions.explanation: Digital tools can capture, label, store, and share sketches so the project idea is communicated clearly.
questions.learningOutcome: Integrate ICT tools with drawing to communicate a project idea.

questions.prompt: In production, what is a material?
options: A substance used to make a product
A person who buys a product
questions.correctAnswer: A substance used to make a product
questions.explanation: Materials such as timber, metal, plastic, fabric, and clay are worked on to produce useful items.
questions.learningOutcome: Define materials used in production.

questions.prompt: Which item is made mainly from a metallic material?
questions.correctAnswer: Steel nail
questions.explanation: Steel is a metal commonly used to make nails, tools, frames, and other strong products.
questions.learningOutcome: Classify common materials as metallic or non-metallic.

questions.prompt: Which property should be considered when choosing material for a school gate?
questions.correctAnswer: Strength
questions.explanation: A gate should be strong enough to resist bending, breaking, and everyday use.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify properties considered when selecting materials for a product.

questions.prompt: Why is it important to select the right material before making a product?
options: The material affects safety, cost, appearance, and durability
The material removes the need for planning
The material makes all tools unnecessary
The material decides the learner's grade automatically
questions.correctAnswer: The material affects safety, cost, appearance, and durability
questions.explanation: Good material selection helps the product work well, last longer, and remain safe for users.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain factors that influence material selection for a product.

questions.prompt: Which material would be most suitable for making a transparent window pane?
questions.correctAnswer: Glass
questions.explanation: Glass is transparent, so it allows light to pass through and is commonly used in windows.
questions.learningOutcome: Match material properties to suitable uses.

questions.prompt: Which group contains only non-metallic materials?
questions.correctAnswer: Plastic, rubber, and timber
questions.explanation: Plastic, rubber, and timber are non-metallic materials used in many household and school products.
questions.learningOutcome: Group common materials according to material type.

questions.prompt: A learner needs a light, waterproof material for a simple pencil case. Which choice is most suitable?
questions.correctAnswer: Plastic sheet
questions.explanation: Plastic sheet is light and resists water better than untreated cardboard or rusted metal.
questions.learningOutcome: Select materials for a simple product based on required properties.

questions.prompt: Which material is a metal?
questions.correctAnswer: Aluminium
questions.explanation: Aluminium is a light metal used in products such as cooking pots, window frames, and cans.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common metallic materials.

questions.prompt: Which property makes copper suitable for electric wires?
questions.correctAnswer: Good electrical conductivity
questions.explanation: Copper allows electric current to flow easily, so it is widely used in wiring.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate properties of metals to their uses.

questions.prompt: What is rusting?
options: Corrosion of iron or steel in the presence of air and moisture
Melting of plastic in hot sun
questions.correctAnswer: Corrosion of iron or steel in the presence of air and moisture
questions.explanation: Rust forms when iron or steel reacts with oxygen and moisture, weakening the metal over time.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain corrosion in common metallic materials.

questions.prompt: Which method can help prevent a steel bicycle frame from rusting?
options: Painting or oiling the exposed metal
Leaving it in rain every night
Washing it with salty water and storing it wet
questions.correctAnswer: Painting or oiling the exposed metal
questions.explanation: Paint or oil forms a barrier that reduces contact between steel, air, and moisture.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply methods used to protect metallic materials from corrosion.

questions.prompt: Which statement best compares steel and aluminium?
options: Steel is generally stronger and heavier, while aluminium is lighter and resists rusting better
Steel is transparent, while aluminium is a type of rubber
Steel is made from paper, while aluminium is made from cloth
Steel and aluminium are both soft plant fibres
questions.correctAnswer: Steel is generally stronger and heavier, while aluminium is lighter and resists rusting better
questions.explanation: Different metals have different properties, so they are selected for different uses.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare properties of common metallic materials.

questions.prompt: Which metal would be suitable for making a cooking pot that should heat quickly and not be too heavy?
questions.correctAnswer: Aluminium
questions.explanation: Aluminium is light and conducts heat well, making it useful for many cooking pots.
questions.learningOutcome: Choose suitable metals for household products based on properties.

questions.prompt: Why should sharp metal offcuts be handled carefully during practical work?
options: They can cut skin and cause injury
They turn into plastic when touched
questions.correctAnswer: They can cut skin and cause injury
questions.explanation: Metal offcuts may have sharp edges, so they should be collected, handled, and disposed of safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Observe safety when handling metallic materials.

questions.prompt: A product must be strong, weather-resistant, and safe for an outdoor school notice frame. Which choice is best justified?
options: Painted steel, because it is strong and the paint helps reduce rusting
Thin paper, because it tears easily
Soft clay, because it dissolves quickly in rain
Cotton wool, because it absorbs water
questions.correctAnswer: Painted steel, because it is strong and the paint helps reduce rusting
questions.explanation: The selected material should match the use and environment; painted steel combines strength with surface protection.
questions.learningOutcome: Justify selection of metallic materials for an outdoor product.

questions.prompt: Which material is non-metallic and comes from trees?
questions.correctAnswer: Timber
questions.explanation: Timber is a natural non-metallic material obtained from trees and used in furniture and construction.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common non-metallic materials.

questions.prompt: Which property makes rubber suitable for handle grips?
options: It is flexible and provides good grip
It conducts electricity better than copper
questions.correctAnswer: It is flexible and provides good grip
questions.explanation: Rubber is flexible and less slippery, so it is useful for grips, soles, and protective coverings.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate properties of non-metallic materials to their uses.

questions.prompt: Which non-metallic material is often used to make water pipes because it is light and does not rust?
questions.correctAnswer: Plastic
questions.explanation: Plastic is light, does not rust, and can be shaped into pipes and fittings.
questions.learningOutcome: Select non-metallic materials for common applications.

questions.prompt: Why should plastic waste from a project be sorted for reuse or proper disposal?
options: To reduce pollution and conserve resources
To make the workshop more dangerous
To hide mistakes from the teacher
To stop learners from measuring accurately
questions.correctAnswer: To reduce pollution and conserve resources
questions.explanation: Sorting and reusing materials supports environmental care and reduces unnecessary waste.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain responsible handling of waste non-metallic materials.

questions.prompt: A learner must choose between glass and plastic for a classroom water bottle. Which comparison is most accurate?
options: Glass is usually more brittle, while plastic is usually lighter and less likely to break
Glass is always flexible, while plastic is always magnetic
Glass rusts in water, while plastic becomes steel
Glass is a metal, while plastic is timber
questions.correctAnswer: Glass is usually more brittle, while plastic is usually lighter and less likely to break
questions.explanation: Glass can break easily when dropped, while many plastics are lighter and more impact-resistant.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare properties of non-metallic materials for a given use.

questions.prompt: Which choice best justifies using plywood for a simple model bridge in class?
options: It is fairly strong, easy to cut, and lighter than many solid metal pieces
It is the best conductor for electric wiring
It is a liquid material that needs no support
It is always transparent like glass
questions.correctAnswer: It is fairly strong, easy to cut, and lighter than many solid metal pieces
questions.explanation: Plywood is a useful non-metallic sheet material for models because it balances strength, weight, and workability.
questions.learningOutcome: Justify selection of a non-metallic material for a simple project.

questions.prompt: Which tool is used to measure short straight distances on a drawing or material?
questions.correctAnswer: Ruler
questions.explanation: A ruler is a measuring tool used for straight lengths and for drawing straight lines.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify basic measuring tools used in production.

questions.prompt: Which tool is best for checking whether two edges meet at a right angle?
questions.correctAnswer: Try square
questions.explanation: A try square checks and marks right angles during measuring and marking out.
questions.learningOutcome: State the use of a try square in marking out.

questions.prompt: Which tool is most suitable for measuring the length around a curved object?
questions.correctAnswer: Flexible tape measure
questions.explanation: A flexible tape measure can bend around curved or large objects to measure their length or circumference.
questions.learningOutcome: Select suitable measuring tools for different measuring tasks.

questions.prompt: Why should measurements be checked before cutting material?
options: To reduce waste and improve accuracy
questions.correctAnswer: To reduce waste and improve accuracy
questions.explanation: Checking measurements before cutting prevents mistakes, saves materials, and improves the final product.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of accurate measuring and marking out.

questions.prompt: Which marking tool is safest for marking a cutting line on a piece of wood in a Grade 7 activity?
questions.correctAnswer: Pencil
questions.explanation: A pencil makes clear marks on wood and is safer for learners than sharp improvised objects.
questions.learningOutcome: Use safe marking tools for simple production tasks.

questions.prompt: A learner marks 20 cm instead of 12 cm on a wooden strip. What is the likely effect?
options: The cut part may be too long and waste material
The tool will automatically correct the mark
The drawing title block will disappear
questions.correctAnswer: The cut part may be too long and waste material
questions.explanation: Wrong measurements lead to poor fitting parts, wasted material, and extra work.
questions.learningOutcome: Predict effects of inaccurate measuring and marking.

questions.prompt: Which sequence is best when preparing to cut a rectangular cardboard piece?
questions.correctAnswer: Measure, mark, check, then cut
questions.explanation: A planned sequence improves accuracy and reduces mistakes during production.
questions.learningOutcome: Sequence measuring and marking out steps for a simple product.

questions.prompt: A learner is making four equal sides for a square frame. Which practice gives the best accuracy?
options: Use the same measuring tool and mark each piece carefully from one end
Use a different unit for every side
Cut all pieces before measuring any side
questions.correctAnswer: Use the same measuring tool and mark each piece carefully from one end
questions.explanation: Consistent measuring from a clear reference point helps the four sides match accurately.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply accurate marking out methods to repeated parts.

questions.prompt: Which tool would help draw a circle on cardboard before cutting a round badge?
questions.correctAnswer: Compass
questions.explanation: A compass is used to draw circles and arcs accurately.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify tools used to mark circles and arcs.

questions.prompt: Which safety rule is most important when carrying pointed marking tools?
options: Carry them with the point facing down and away from others
Run while waving them above the head
Place them inside a pocket with the point upward
Throw them to a classmate across the room
questions.correctAnswer: Carry them with the point facing down and away from others
questions.explanation: Pointed tools can injure people, so they must be carried calmly and directed away from the body.
questions.learningOutcome: Observe safety when handling marking out tools.

questions.prompt: A class wants to make identical name tags. Which method is most efficient?
options: Prepare one accurate template and mark each tag from it
Draw each tag at random sizes
Cut all pieces before drawing any shape
Use a wet string instead of a measuring tool
questions.correctAnswer: Prepare one accurate template and mark each tag from it
questions.explanation: A template helps repeat the same shape and size quickly and accurately.
questions.learningOutcome: Use simple templates to improve consistency in production.

questions.prompt: Which statement best explains tolerance in a simple production task?
options: A small acceptable variation from the required measurement
A rule that measurements should never be checked
A method of turning timber into glass
questions.correctAnswer: A small acceptable variation from the required measurement
questions.explanation: Tolerance recognises that small variations may occur, but parts must still fit and function properly.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain acceptable accuracy in simple production measurements.

questions.prompt: A learner must mark screw positions equally along a 24 cm strip, leaving 6 cm between positions. Which set is suitable?
questions.correctAnswer: 6 cm, 12 cm, 18 cm, and 24 cm
questions.explanation: Equal spacing of 6 cm gives positions at 6, 12, 18, and 24 cm along the strip.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply equal spacing when marking out positions on a material.

questions.prompt: Which marking plan would best reduce waste when cutting several small rectangles from one cardboard sheet?
options: Arrange the rectangles close together before cutting and leave only needed margins
Cut from random places across the sheet
Leave a large empty gap around every rectangle
Tear the sheet into pieces before measuring
questions.correctAnswer: Arrange the rectangles close together before cutting and leave only needed margins
questions.explanation: Careful layout uses material efficiently while leaving enough space for safe cutting.
questions.learningOutcome: Plan material layout to reduce waste during marking out.

questions.prompt: Which computer hardware displays text, pictures, and videos to the user?
questions.correctAnswer: Monitor
questions.explanation: A monitor is an output device that shows visual information from the computer.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common computer output hardware.

questions.prompt: Which hardware device is used to point, click, and select items on a computer screen?
questions.correctAnswer: Mouse
questions.explanation: A mouse is an input device that controls the pointer and helps users select commands.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify common computer input hardware.

questions.prompt: What is the main function of a printer?
options: To produce a hard copy from digital work
questions.correctAnswer: To produce a hard copy from digital work
questions.explanation: A printer changes digital text or images into printed output on paper or similar media.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the function of common output devices.

questions.prompt: Which hardware device can capture a paper drawing and turn it into a digital file?
questions.correctAnswer: Scanner
questions.explanation: A scanner converts printed or drawn material into a digital image file.
questions.learningOutcome: Select hardware for converting physical work into digital form.

questions.prompt: Why should food and drinks be kept away from computer hardware?
options: Spills and crumbs can damage devices and cause faults
questions.correctAnswer: Spills and crumbs can damage devices and cause faults
questions.explanation: Liquids and dirt can damage circuits, keys, and moving parts in computer hardware.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain safe care practices for computer hardware.

questions.prompt: A computer does not start after the power cable is unplugged. What should the learner do first?
options: Report to the teacher and check power connection under guidance
questions.correctAnswer: Report to the teacher and check power connection under guidance
questions.explanation: Learners should follow safe troubleshooting steps and avoid opening electrical equipment without supervision.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply safe basic troubleshooting for computer hardware.

questions.prompt: Who is an entrepreneur?
options: A person who identifies an opportunity and organises resources to provide goods or services
A person who never takes responsibility for work
A person who only consumes products without creating value
A person who hides business records
questions.correctAnswer: A person who identifies an opportunity and organises resources to provide goods or services
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs solve needs by organising resources, taking risk, and offering goods or services.
questions.learningOutcome: Define entrepreneurship and the role of an entrepreneur.

questions.prompt: Which quality is important for a young entrepreneur?
questions.correctAnswer: Honesty
questions.explanation: Honesty builds trust with customers, team members, and suppliers.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify values and qualities of entrepreneurs.

questions.prompt: Which example is a service rather than a good?
questions.correctAnswer: Repairing a torn school bag
questions.explanation: A service is work done for someone, while a good is a physical item that can be sold or used.
questions.learningOutcome: Differentiate between goods and services in entrepreneurship.

questions.prompt: A group notices that learners need affordable pencil holders. What entrepreneurial step should come first?
options: Identify the need clearly and discuss possible solutions
Borrow money before knowing the product
Make many items without asking users
Hide the idea from all group members
questions.correctAnswer: Identify the need clearly and discuss possible solutions
questions.explanation: A good enterprise starts by understanding the need, users, resources, and possible solutions.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify simple entrepreneurial opportunities in the school environment.

questions.prompt: Which action best shows good customer care during a school sale?
options: Listening politely and explaining the product clearly
Laughing at customers who ask questions
Changing prices secretly for friends only
questions.correctAnswer: Listening politely and explaining the product clearly
questions.explanation: Good customer care uses respect, clear communication, and fairness to build trust.
questions.learningOutcome: Demonstrate customer care in simple entrepreneurial activities.

questions.prompt: Which risk should a learner consider before producing many handmade bookmarks for sale?
options: Some learners may not buy them if the design or price is unsuitable
Bookmarks will automatically sell at any price
questions.correctAnswer: Some learners may not buy them if the design or price is unsuitable
questions.explanation: Entrepreneurs consider demand, price, quality, and customer preferences before producing many items.
questions.learningOutcome: Assess simple risks in an entrepreneurial idea.

questions.prompt: What is a production unit in a school project?
options: An organised place or group where goods or services are produced
A random pile of unused materials
A password used to open a file
A drawing with no plan for making anything
questions.correctAnswer: An organised place or group where goods or services are produced
questions.explanation: A production unit brings people, tools, materials, and processes together to produce an output.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe a production unit and its purpose.

questions.prompt: Which set contains the main inputs for producing a simple pencil holder?
options: Materials, tools, labour, time, and money
questions.correctAnswer: Materials, tools, labour, time, and money
questions.explanation: Production needs resources such as materials, tools, people, time, and sometimes money.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify inputs used in a simple production unit.

questions.prompt: A group plans to make ten dustbins from plastic containers. Which arrangement supports efficient production?
options: Assign roles for cleaning, marking, cutting, finishing, and checking quality
Let everyone cut randomly at the same time
Skip safety checks to finish quickly
Start selling before any item is complete
questions.correctAnswer: Assign roles for cleaning, marking, cutting, finishing, and checking quality
questions.explanation: Clear roles and a planned workflow improve safety, speed, teamwork, and product quality.
questions.learningOutcome: Organise roles in a simple production unit.

questions.prompt: Why should a production unit check quality before selling products?
options: To ensure the products are safe, useful, and acceptable to customers
To make all products more expensive without reason
questions.correctAnswer: To ensure the products are safe, useful, and acceptable to customers
questions.explanation: Quality checks help identify defects, protect users, and maintain trust in the product.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the importance of quality control in production.

questions.prompt: A production group has limited cardboard but many orders for desk organisers. What is the best decision?
options: Plan the layout carefully, prioritise confirmed orders, and avoid waste
Cut shapes randomly until the cardboard ends
Promise every buyer without checking materials
Throw away small usable offcuts immediately
questions.correctAnswer: Plan the layout carefully, prioritise confirmed orders, and avoid waste
questions.explanation: Good production decisions balance demand, available resources, efficiency, and honesty with customers.
questions.learningOutcome: Make production decisions when resources are limited.

questions.prompt: What is a financial goal?
options: A money target a person plans to achieve
questions.correctAnswer: A money target a person plans to achieve
questions.explanation: A financial goal gives direction for saving, spending, and planning money wisely.
questions.learningOutcome: Define a financial goal.

questions.prompt: Which financial goal is specific and measurable?
options: Save KES 300 in six weeks to buy project materials
questions.correctAnswer: Save KES 300 in six weeks to buy project materials
questions.explanation: A clear goal states the amount, purpose, and time, making progress easier to track.
questions.learningOutcome: Write simple specific and measurable financial goals.

questions.prompt: A learner earns KES 500 from selling bookmarks and spends KES 350 on materials and transport. How much is left?
questions.correctAnswer: KES 150
questions.explanation: The amount left is income minus expenses: 500 - 350 = 150.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate money left after simple expenses.

questions.prompt: Which budget choice best supports a learner's financial goal to buy a drawing set?
options: Record income, set aside savings first, then plan necessary spending
Spend first and save only if money remains by chance
questions.correctAnswer: Record income, set aside savings first, then plan necessary spending
questions.explanation: Budgeting helps a learner direct money toward the goal while still meeting necessary expenses.
questions.learningOutcome: Use budgeting decisions to support financial goals.

questions.prompt: A group wants to save for better tools while still buying materials for current orders. Which plan is strongest?
options: Set a savings target, estimate material costs, price products fairly, and review records weekly
Use all sales money for snacks and hope tools appear later
Stop recording expenses because records take time
Raise prices randomly without checking costs or customers
questions.correctAnswer: Set a savings target, estimate material costs, price products fairly, and review records weekly
questions.explanation: A strong financial plan links goals, costs, pricing, records, and regular review.
questions.learningOutcome: Create a simple financial plan that balances saving and production needs.
